extracted.intended_audience: Emergency Responders/Receivers, Law Enforcement, Public Information/Media Specialists, Emergency Management, Public Safety Communications
extracted.subtask_description: A 2-day (16-hour) classroom course (G290) teaching foundational Public Information Officer skills: NIMS/ICS roles, single- and multi-PIO incident communications, JIS vs JIC, triggers for JIC activation, and partnership-building strategies; emphasizes skills development and the impact of technology on emergency public information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe why public informaition officers train at this level
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe why public informaition officers train at this level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the course learning objectives; the course is an updated, shortened and revised 2-day classroom course with emphasis on skills development and addresses the impact of technology on emergency public information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define NIMS and explain where public information fits in
rubrics_metrics.description: Define NIMS, and explain where public information fits in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students should be able to state what NIMS is and articulate the placement and responsibilities of public information within the NIMS framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define ICS and the role of the PIO within ICS
rubrics_metrics.description: Define ICS and the role of the PIO within ICS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction includes the Incident Command System structure and the specific duties, reporting relationships, and expectations for a Public Information Officer operating within ICS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyse communications needs of a single-PIO incident
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyse the communications needs of a single-PIO incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learners should assess information flow, media/public interaction, workload, and message consistency when only one PIO is assigned to an incident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe advantages and disadvantages of working with multiple PIOs
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe advantages and disadvantages of working with multiple PIOs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate coordination challenges, message control, resource sharing, and benefits such as broader coverage and role specialization when multiple PIOs are involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate between the the JIS and JIC
rubrics_metrics.description: Differentiate between the the JIS and JIC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify definitions, purposes, structures, and operational differences between a Joint Information System (JIS) and a Joint Information Center (JIC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe triggers for JIC activation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify incident characteristics, stakeholder needs, and resource thresholds that should prompt establishment of a JIC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify strategies for building partnerships as all levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify strategies for building partnerships as all levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop approaches for relationship-building across local, state, tribal, and federal partners and with media and community organizations (note: original text reads 'as all levels').

rubrics_metrics.name: Course length requirement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The G290 offering is a 16-hour, 2-day classroom-format course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisite
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students must have completed IS-29 prior to attending this course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target audience/discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Target Audience/Discipline: Emergency Responders/Receivers, Law Enforcement, Public Information/Media Specialist, Emergency Management, Public Safety Communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course is intended for practitioners in emergency response, law enforcement, PIO/media roles, emergency management, and public safety communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration timing and walk-in policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Please note: Applications for courses will be accepted up to 1 day prior to the course date. Registration should be made in advance to attend any IEMA sponsored class. Walk-in registrations are only accepted if room space and course materials are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must register in advance; last-day registration allowed up to one day before; walk-ins depend on available space and materials.

rubrics_metrics.description: To register for IEMA classes, please see the IEMA Online Registration and Tracking Program Page. If you want to learn more about the Training Program or are interested in attending a specific course, please contact your IEMA Regional Coordinator or Nancy Buck.
